questions.text: What's the best thing you've ever made with your hands? Photos encouraged.
What half-finished project is sitting somewhere in your home right now, judging you?
What did you teach yourself with no help, and how bad were the early attempts?
What's the one tool — any trade, any hobby — you'd never lend to anyone?
Show us or describe your very first attempt at something you're now decent at.
What hobby has cost you the most money, and was it worth every penny?
What have you repaired that everyone told you to throw away?
What skill do you have that almost never comes up? When did it last save the day?
What are you planning to learn next, and what's the first step you haven't taken yet?
What practical skill do you think is dying out that people should keep alive?
What did someone in your family teach you that you'd pass on?
Do you finish things or endlessly refine them? What's the last thing you actually called done?
Describe your workspace — garage, desk, kitchen table. Is it organised chaos or actual chaos?
What are you building or working on right now that nobody asked you to?
What project failed so completely that it became funny? Walk us through the wreckage.
Have you ever sold something you made? What was it, and how did the first sale feel?
What supplies are you hoarding for a project you might never start?
What's the best improvised fix you've ever pulled off with completely the wrong materials?
Do you plan a project on paper first or just start and find out? Which has burned you?
What's the best thing you've made as a gift, and how did they react?
What have you learned entirely from watching other people do it online?
What mistake in something you made did you decide to keep because it looked better?
What piece of equipment would immediately change what you're able to make?
Do you write, draw, build, code, or cook to get thoughts out of your head? Which one is your outlet?
What technique took you the longest to get right, and what finally made it click?
How do you handle criticism of something you made? Has that changed over time?
Have you ever made something with someone else? Did the collaboration work?
What activity makes four hours disappear without you noticing?
What could you teach a complete beginner in an hour?
Where do you deliberately cut corners, and where will you never compromise?
What was the first serious piece of kit you bought for a hobby, and do you still have it?
If you could restore one old, broken, or neglected thing, what would you take on?
Do you sign, name, or date what you make? Why or why not?
Tell us about a project you nearly binned and then rescued.
Do you get more satisfaction from something physical or something digital? Which one lasts longer?
What have you made small that you'd love to make enormous, given the space and budget?
Would you turn your hobby into a job? What would that ruin about it?
Has a stranger online ever helped you finish something? What did they do?
Do you follow the pattern, recipe, or plan exactly, or start modifying immediately?
Do you own any tools or equipment that belonged to someone else first? What's the story?
